title.narrative: Supporting Rwanda Towards Reducing TB and HIV-related Morbidity and Mortality - Rwanda (01-Jul-2024-30-Jun-2027)

description.narrative: Rwanda, TB/HIV, Ministry of Health of the Republic of Rwanda (Ministry of health)This program has the following goals: Reducing new HIV infections by 15% in 2027. Reduce HIV-related deaths by 2027 and decrease HIV morbidity. People infected and affected by HIV have the same opportunities as the general population. End the tuberculosis epidemic in Rwanda by 2035 which means 10 incident cases per 100 000 population or less per year (new and relapses).. 65% reduction in TB deaths (compared with 2015). 33% reduction in TB incidence rate (compared with 2015). Reduction of TB-affected families facing catastrophic costs due to TB (to be determined (TBD) after the survey). The objectives of this program are: New HIV infections transmitted through sexual intercourse are reduced. Most at risk populations have access to combined HIV and Sexual Reproductive health prevention services. People access and use services to eliminate mother to child transmission of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis. Maintain blood safety to enforce universal precautions for HIV, Hepatitis, and Syphilis . ART coverage and retention in care among all age categories of PLHIV is above 95%. Viral Load suppression among all PLHIV on ART is maintained above 95%. Reduced HIV morbidity and mortality related co-infections among PLHIV. Improved Psychosocial wellbeing for optimal and effective response to ART. Socioeconomic status for infected and affected people living with HIV is improved. Ensure social and legal protection of people infected and affected by HIV.. Stigma and discrimination related to HIV is reduced.. Social harm and violence among people infected and affected by HIV and key population are halted. Considering the patient pathway for tuberculosis. Targeted approaches for key drivers of TB epidemic among selected populations. Programmatic management, Multi-Sectoral collaboration & engaging all care providers. Universal Health Coverage, social protection, human rights & nutrition. Stable and quality assured supply of drugs, diagnostic and commodities
